anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
## (1) First message

The premise check found one contradiction. Ticket row 2 says "The export includes the owner column." The table contract has no owner column: `src/export/csv.ts:40` defines `const tableColumns = ["title", "status"];`. The draft says the CSV export reuses those column definitions, so an export built on that contract today would produce only title and status. The design continues on that fact, and you can override it in your reply.

The other premises are less certain:
- **Reports page has no export action.** This comes from the gather draft only. I have not read the reports page component, so I have not confirmed it.
- **Export reuses the table's columns.** This is the draft's claim. Line 40 is the only part of `csv.ts` I have seen, so I have not traced how the serializer reads `tableColumns`, and I have not found its callers.
- **Owner data on report rows.** I don't know whether report rows carry an owner field at all.
- **Speed of a 10k-row export.** I don't know whether the existing serialization and paging can export 10k rows in under 60s.

These open points go to Open Questions. None of them stops the design.

The framing holds. I checked:
- the column contract at `src/export/csv.ts:40`
- the draft's report that the page renders a table with no export action, so the ask is not already solved
- the scout's owner-column objection, which names a mismatch but no alternative to adding an export, so it is a lead to settle in approaches, not a framing concern

I'm recording `Framing: kept`.

Where should the Export CSV button appear?
- **A)** beside the report title
- **B)** in a toolbar directly above the table
- **C)** inside an existing page-actions or overflow menu

Recommendation: A. The page has no export action and, as far as the draft shows, no actions menu. A visible button beside the title meets row 1 without creating a new UI container.

---

## (2) Approaches message

The button goes beside the report title, as you answered. What separates the options below is how much changes beyond wiring that button to the existing serializer:
- nothing
- the shared column contract
- the execution model

**Recommended: A. Reuse the existing CSV serializer and paging unchanged, and add only the button.**
- The button sits beside the report title and calls the existing serializer, which emits the table's columns (`title`, `status`).
- Row 2 becomes `deviates: the table contract (src/export/csv.ts:40) has no owner column, and the export reuses that contract`.
- Choosing A is also your decision on that row. The shipped CSV will have no owner column, which differs from what the ticket says the user will see.
- Row 3 stays `in-scope`. The plan adds a 10k-row export test that must finish under 60s, using the existing paging.
- This is the minimal reuse-only option, with no new construct.

`Pattern: follows the shared column contract at src/export/csv.ts:40 - the export stays a projection of the table.`

**B. Reuse the serializer and paging, and add `owner` to the shared `tableColumns`.**
- Row 2 stays `in-scope`, and the export and table stay on one contract.
- The cost is that the reports table on screen also gains an owner column, which the ticket does not ask for.
- It also requires owner data on report rows, which I have not verified.

`Pattern: extends the owning contract at src/export/csv.ts:40 rather than forking it; sound, but widens the change to the visible table.`

**C. Drop the ask's assumption that the export runs inline when the button is clicked.**
- The button starts a server-side export job and delivers a file when it finishes. This makes the 60s target easier to meet for large reports.
- It needs a job runner, status polling, and file delivery that the repo shows no sign of.
- The owner column would still need A's deviation or B's contract change.

`Pattern: introduces a new async execution path beside the existing serializer and paging in src/export/csv.ts; justified only if inline export cannot meet the bound.`

**Rejected: an export-only column list that adds `owner` without touching the table.** I'm not offering this. It would be a second column contract beside the one that owns them at `csv.ts:40`, so table and export could drift.

**What would flip the recommendation:**
- If report rows already carry an owner field and showing it on the table is acceptable, B ships row 2 as written for a one-line contract change, and B becomes the pick.
- If the 10k-row test shows that the existing paging cannot finish under 60s, C becomes necessary.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
## 1. First message to the user

The framing holds on the supplied evidence: I checked the table-column definition at `src/export/csv.ts:40` against the ticket’s export requirements; the page’s callers, serializer inputs, paging path, and available owner data cannot be traced from the provided fixture.

One correction to the gather draft: `["title", "status"]` establishes the current columns, but does not establish that exporting an owner column is prohibited. I’ll keep all three ticket acceptance criteria in scope. The reported absence of an export action and the availability of reusable serialization and paging remain unverified; the 10k-row performance requirement will need measurement.

Where should the Export CSV button appear?

A) Beside the report title.  
B) In the table toolbar.  
C) Other — name it.

Recommendation: A - it makes the report-level action visible without placing it among row-level controls.

## 2. Approaches message

I recommend **reusing the existing CSV serializer and paging, with an explicit export column selection that includes owner**. This matches your recorded implementation choice, and the button will appear beside the report title.

The approaches differ in **whether the owner requirement changes only the export or also changes the displayed table**.

**A) Reuse the serializer and paging; configure the export columns separately.**  
Keep the displayed table unchanged. Reuse its title/status definitions where supported, and include owner in the export selection. Export every page of the report, rather than only the currently displayed page, and measure a representative 10k-row export against the ticket’s under-60-second requirement.

This is the minimal reuse-only candidate **if the existing serializer accepts configurable columns and paging supplies owner data**. Those capabilities are assumptions to verify, not facts established by the fixture. Avoid duplicating formatting definitions or introducing a second paging implementation.

Pattern: follows the reported reuse of table definitions in `src/export/csv.ts`; the selection differs because the ticket explicitly requires a field absent from `tableColumns` at line 40.

**B) Add owner to the shared table/export column contract, then reuse serialization and paging unchanged.**  
This drops the assumption that the displayed table must remain title/status-only. Adding owner to the shared definitions could preserve identical table and export columns, but it also changes the reports UI beyond the requested export action. It is appropriate only if showing owner in the table is a desired product outcome and the existing rendering/data path supports it.

Pattern: preserves the reported shared-column convention in `src/export/csv.ts`, but broadens the user-visible table contract defined at line 40.

The recorded choice favors A. I would switch to B only if owner should also appear in the table—not merely because the current serializer makes an export-specific selection inconvenient. If the reuse assumptions fail, the design needs revisiting rather than silently omitting owner or relaxing the performance criterion.
